title: Planning-run expansion submission
description: Objective: enable the existing authoritative PlanningRun reducer to process exactly bound EXPANSION drafts and compound plan.propose submissions without weakening INITIAL behavior. Depends on task-fcad40b6d26243439cd19fd3e49c924d. Deliverable: PlanningRun validates the active hold-bound EXPANSION schema, seals one immutable multi-node proposal/refusal, and remains zero-authority until later approval. NOT in scope: REVISION support, scheduler admission, automatic approval, resource/budget preparation, graph activation, or persistence. Owned paths: packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-reducer.ts, planning-run-submission.ts, planning-run-reducer.test.ts. Production consumers: scheduler/core expansion children and task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test.
definitionOfDone: PlanningRun accepts EXPANSION creation/proposal only when the exact active hold, parent/handoff, proposal-base hash, goal version, graph epoch, planning authority, and finalized runner boundary match; REVISION remains explicitly unsupported.

The compound submission seals the complete child/integrator proposal identity or one stable expansion refusal; malformed, stale, wrong-kind, mismatched-hold, incomplete, or changed multi-node inputs refuse with exact code and layer and leave state unchanged.

INITIAL behavior and its single-node fence remain unchanged, and no EXPANSION accepted/refused result contains child run, lease, effect, slot, resource, budget allocation, graph activation, dispatch, or partial proposal authority.

Focused tests cover INITIAL compatibility, EXPANSION success, duplicate replay, refusal precedence, changed base/epoch/hold, competing finalize/cancel schedules, nonzero generated permutations, and production guard mutations with exact code plus layer.
The exact verification command exits 0, production files remain below 400 lines, and the named downstream consumers are recorded.
taskRails: Extend the existing PlanningRun authority; do not implement a parallel expansion submission reducer.
One sealed proposal is all-or-none and immutable.
Manual review remains required after submission.

implementationPlan.description: Baseline before writing a byte. Confirm the dependency surface is committed and clean: `git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only -- packages/core/src/planning/planning-expansion-validation.ts` and `git status --porcelain -- packages/core/src/planning packages/core/src/expansion` (must be EMPTY). Run the owned-package gate FIRST and record it: `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test`. An empty diff at this moment is what proves any later red is yours. Record physical line counts with `grep -c ''` for the 5 existing owned files (measured 2026-08-09: planning-run-reducer 192, planning-run-submission 186, planning-results 121, planning-run-test-fixtures 156, planning-run-reducer.test 228). NOTE the task's own DoD 5 says 'below 400 lines' — that is WRONG for these paths: planning-source-size.test.ts hard-caps every .ts in src/planning at 250 physical lines with no allowlist and sweeps tests, fixtures and drivers equally. Treat 250 as the bar.

RED first (TDD). Create packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-expansion.test.ts driving the PRODUCTION reducer — never a helper that reimplements validation. It must fail for the right reason before any production edit: today reducer.ts:77 and submission.ts:52 both answer unsupported('PLANNING_KIND_UNSUPPORTED') for every non-INITIAL kind. Cover: (a) an EXPANSION create_draft carrying a valid hold binding is ACCEPTED and lands DRAFT with runKind EXPANSION, the hold binding on state, and sealedProposal null; (b) REVISION create_draft still answers exactly `{ ok: false, reason: 'PLANNING_KIND_UNSUPPORTED', unsupported: true }` — assert the whole discriminated shape, not just ok===false; (c) an EXPANSION plan.propose whose sealedProposal binds submissionHash and witness.submissionRef seals and emits PlanningSubmissionSealed carrying proposalKind EXPANSION; (d) a mismatched sealedProposal.proposalHash, a cross-kind carrier (INITIAL command carrying an `expansion` key), a stale proposalBaseHash, a non-ACTIVE hold lifecycle and a wrong graphEpoch each refuse with exact ILLEGAL_TRANSITION and details `{ aggregateKind: 'PLANNING_RUN', commandKind, sourceState }`; (e) duplicate replay of the same EXPANSION submissionHash is accepted idempotently with no new event, exactly as the INITIAL path at submission.ts:53-56; (f) a multi-node EXPANSION finalize with child + integrator nodes SEALS instead of refusing; (g) every refusal leaves input state byte-identical (JSON.stringify before/after). Keep this file at or below 250 physical lines.

Fixtures. In planning-run-test-fixtures.ts add deterministic EXPANSION builders so neither test file reimplements the schema: a valid PlanningExpansionHoldBinding (all 11 keys per planning-expansion-validation.ts:57-60 — generation, goalVersion, graphEpoch, holdId, lifecycle 'ACTIVE', parentNodeRef, parentRunRef, proposalBaseHash, sourceFingerprint, truthClass 'DAEMON_VERIFIED', workerHandoff {digest, ref}), a valid PlanningExpansionProposalIdentity (proposalHash, proposalRef, truthClass), an EXPANSION create command, an EXPANSION propose command whose sealedProposal.proposalHash === submissionHash and sealedProposal.proposalRef === witness.submissionRef, and a multi-node finalize witness with one child and one integrator node both executionBearing. Add named MALFORMED variants for each refusal case in step 2 so the tests select a fixture rather than hand-mutating inline. Existing INITIAL fixtures must not change — planning-run-authority.test.ts and planning-run-reducer.test.ts both consume this file. Budget ~30 lines against 94 free.

Reducer: admit EXPANSION creation and, critically, make EXPANSION state readable. In planning-run-reducer.ts: (1) THE LOAD-BEARING LINE — :178 currently calls `snapshotPlanningRunState(state)` from planning-validation.ts, whose `exact()` guard accepts ONLY the 12-key legacy shape, so an EXPANSION state (14 keys) returns undefined and every command against it degrades to unknownFailure(). Replace it with `snapshotPlanningRunContractState` from ./planning-expansion-validation.js, which accepts the legacy shape AND the EXPANSION shape and is already root-published. Without this change nothing else in this task can work. (2) In create(), keep `if (!validRunKind(command.runKind)) return unknownFailure()`, keep REVISION answering unsupported('PLANNING_KIND_UNSUPPORTED'), and add an EXPANSION branch that validates the whole command with the production `validExpansionCreateCommand` (do not re-derive its predicates) and builds the 14-key state: the existing 12 fields plus `expansion` (the hold binding, deep-frozen) and `sealedProposal: null`. A malformed EXPANSION command returns unknownFailure() from the create path, matching how the INITIAL path already treats malformed creation input. Emit PlanningRunCreated carrying `expansion` so validExpansionCreatedEvent accepts it. Budget ~14 lines against 58 free.

Submission: admit EXPANSION proposals. In planning-run-submission.ts propose(): keep the existing INITIAL path byte-identical, keep REVISION answering unsupported('PLANNING_KIND_UNSUPPORTED'), and add an EXPANSION branch validated by the production `validExpansionProposeCommand` — which already enforces that sealedProposal.proposalHash equals submissionHash and sealedProposal.proposalRef equals witness.submissionRef (planning-expansion-validation.ts:132-133). Do NOT restate those two equalities in the reducer or in a test helper; compose the predicate. On acceptance seal `sealedProposal` onto the state alongside submissionHash, and emit PlanningSubmissionSealed carrying `expansion`, `proposalKind` and `sealedProposal` so validExpansionSealedEvent accepts it. The duplicate-replay branch at :53-56 must behave identically for EXPANSION: same submissionHash replays as accepted with no new event, a different one is illegal. A malformed EXPANSION command returns illegal(state, command.kind), consistent with every other malformed witness on this aggregate. Budget ~16 lines against 64 free.

Submission: lift the multi-node fence for EXPANSION only. planning-run-submission.ts finalize() at :96 answers unsupported('MULTI_NODE_EXECUTION_UNSUPPORTED', bearing) whenever more than one node is executionBearing. EXPANSION is inherently multi-node — DoD 2 requires sealing the complete child/integrator proposal identity — so this fence must apply to INITIAL only. Condition it on the run kind, NOT on the node count: `state.runKind !== 'EXPANSION' && bearing.length > 1` refuses exactly as today. `bearing.length === 0` stays illegal for BOTH kinds — a proposal that bears no execution is malformed regardless of kind. DoD 3 is explicit that INITIAL's single-node fence is unchanged, so the existing assertion at planning-run-reducer.test.ts:180 must stay green untouched; if it reddens, the condition is wrong. Update the doc comment at :73-77 to say the fence is INITIAL-scoped and why. Budget ~4 lines.

Close the successor defect this task would otherwise ship. planning-results.ts successorData() at :96-105 builds a 12-key literal with `runKind: state.runKind`. Once EXPANSION runs exist, rejecting one (via finalize's refusal branch at submission.ts:92, or plan.revise at :134) produces a successor claiming runKind EXPANSION with no `expansion` and no `sealedProposal` — a state `validExpansionContractState` rejects outright, so the next command against it degrades to unknownFailure(). Carry the predecessor's `expansion` hold binding onto an EXPANSION successor and set `sealedProposal: null` (a successor has sealed nothing). Keep building from literals, never by spreading the rejected run's objects — the doc comment at :95 says why, and a test must assert the successor does not alias the predecessor's binding object. INITIAL and REVISION successors must remain byte-identical. Add a test in the step-2 file: reject an EXPANSION run, then confirm the successor is accepted by `snapshotPlanningRunContractState` and that a follow-up command against it does NOT return UNKNOWN_ERROR. Budget ~8 lines against 129 free.

Update ONLY the assertions the new behavior genuinely invalidates in planning-run-reducer.test.ts; every other assertion in the 228-line file must pass untouched, and there are only ~22 lines of headroom so do not grow it. (a) :44-47 — create_draft with runKind 'EXPANSION' currently expects `{ reason: 'PLANNING_KIND_UNSUPPORTED', unsupported: true }`. EXPANSION creation is now legal: narrow this case to REVISION only. (b) :132-137 'refuses REVISION and EXPANSION proposals with the typed UNSUPPORTED variant' — the loop `for (const proposalKind of ['REVISION', 'EXPANSION'])` is now half false. Narrow the loop to REVISION and rename the test to say REVISION. Do NOT delete either case: REVISION must still be provably unsupported, and a test that stops asserting it is how REVISION silently becomes reachable. DO NOT TOUCH :180 (MULTI_NODE_EXECUTION_UNSUPPORTED on the INITIAL path — DoD 3 requires it green unchanged) or anything in planning-run-authority.test.ts, which has no EXPANSION or KIND_UNSUPPORTED assertions and must not be edited at all.

Mutation drills, then restore byte-exact. Each must redden a NAMED test in an owned file, and must target a guard THIS task added — reddening a dependency-owned predicate proves nothing about this transition. Drill and record the failing test name for each: (a) reducer.ts — revert the snapshot call to `snapshotPlanningRunState` and confirm EXPANSION commands degrade to UNKNOWN_ERROR (this proves the load-bearing line is actually load-bearing); (b) drop `validExpansionCreateCommand` from the create branch and confirm a malformed hold binding is accepted; (c) drop `validExpansionProposeCommand` from propose and confirm a mismatched sealedProposal.proposalHash is accepted; (d) change the finalize fence to `bearing.length > 1` unconditionally and confirm the multi-node EXPANSION seal test reddens; (e) change it to skip the fence entirely and confirm the INITIAL assertion at reducer.test.ts:180 reddens — both directions, because a fence that never fires and a fence that always fires are different bugs; (f) revert successorData to drop `expansion` and confirm the successor test reddens. Two shared-worktree hazards: `git diff` is BLIND to the new untracked test file, so never verify its restoration by an empty diff — hash it before and after; and a foreign whole-tree completion hook can COMMIT your drill edit, after which git status looks clean while the mutation is live — re-run the suite after every restore.

Verify, self-review, complete. (1) Hand-measure every touched .ts with `grep -c ''` and confirm all 6 are at or below 250 — not the 400 the task's DoD 5 wrongly states; PowerShell Measure-Object -Line skips blank lines and will report headroom you do not have. planning-run-reducer.test.ts started at 228 and must not have grown past 250. (2) Run the exact DoD command fresh and last, unnarrowed, with no path filter: `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test`. Read the Test Files count, not just the tail — a narrowed or mistyped invocation reads as green. (3) Path-attributed baseline: run repo-wide `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` at merge-base and at HEAD; the known foreign red is packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts ('unterminated regular expression source token' on apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts, a pre-existing shebang tokenizer defect). Disclose it verbatim, never call it green and never claim it as yours; the owned-package legs must still be exit 0. (4) Adversarial self-review of your own diff: does any EXPANSION accepted or refused result carry child-run, lease, effect, slot, resource, budget-allocation, graph-activation, dispatch or partial-proposal authority (DoD 3 forbids all of them)? Is REVISION still provably unsupported on BOTH the create and propose paths? Did narrowing the two loops in step 8 leave anything untested? Does any test assert only ok===false rather than the exact discriminated shape? (5) Record the named downstream consumers per DoD 5 — task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2 and the scheduler/core expansion children — in your completion notes. (6) Stage and commit ONLY the 6 owned paths by explicit pathspec; never git add -A.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED changing PlanningRunState into a discriminated union. That is the obvious way to model EXPANSION's two extra keys, and it is already recorded as WRONG in production: planning-event-contract.ts:47-57 says a union there 'produces a cross-product whose mixed members are unassignable, which breaks planning-results.ts and planning-run-test-fixtures.ts — measured, not assumed'. `PlanningRunContractState` is deliberately `PlanningRunState & {...}` so it WIDENS to PlanningRunState and `clonedState`'s `Partial<PlanningRunState>` spread keeps working. Consequence for this plan: no type change is needed anywhere. planning-contract.ts and planning-event-contract.ts stay untouched, and the entire EXPANSION admission is a runtime-validation swap plus two branches.

REJECTED adding a layer discriminant to the planning-run result, which is what I did on the sibling graph-revision aggregate for the same DoD wording. Measurement shows it is unnecessary here and would be a second vocabulary: (a) `illegal()` already puts `aggregateKind: 'PLANNING_RUN'` in `details`, which survives sanitizeDetails because ILLEGAL_TRANSITION declares those detail keys — unlike REVISION_REBOUND, which is NO_KEY and forced the discriminant on the other aggregate; (b) `unsupported()` results carry `unsupported: true` plus a typed `reason`, which is itself the discriminant; (c) the dependency already ships exact code AND layer via `inspectPlanningExpansionContract` returning `{ code: PLANNING_EXPANSION_*_INVALID, layer: BINDING|IDENTITY|COMMAND|EVENT|STATE|TARGET }`. Compose those three; mint nothing.

REJECTED gating the multi-node fence on node count or on a new flag. Gating on `state.runKind !== 'EXPANSION'` keeps INITIAL's fence provably byte-equivalent, which is what DoD 3 demands, and keeps the zero-bearing case illegal for both kinds.

REJECTED squeezing the new coverage into planning-run-reducer.test.ts. It is 228 lines against a hard 250 cap enforced by planning-source-size.test.ts, so 22 lines cannot hold DoD 4's eight required scenarios. A focused new file is the only option that does not force shrinking existing assertions.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE TASK'S OWN DoD 5 IS WRONG. It says 'production files remain below 400 lines'. Both owned production files live in packages/core/src/planning, which planning-source-size.test.ts hard-caps at 250 physical lines — no allowlist, no basename exception, tests and fixtures swept equally. Building to 400 there fails the suite. 250 is the bar; the DoD text is the defect.

2. THE SILENT-DEGRADE FAILURE MODE. If the snapshot swap at reducer.ts:178 is missed, EXPANSION states fail the 12-key `exact()` guard and every command returns unknownFailure() — no exception, no obviously wrong code, just UNKNOWN_ERROR. A test asserting only ok===false would pass while nothing works. Assert the full discriminated shape on every refusal, and run drill (a).

3. SUCCESSOR DEFECT, easy to ship unnoticed. successorData() builds a 12-key literal with `runKind: state.runKind`. Rejecting an EXPANSION run yields a state claiming EXPANSION with no hold binding — invalid, and only observable on the NEXT command. Step 7 closes it; without that step the task is completable and wrong.

4. NARROWING A LOOP IS NOT UPDATING A TEST. Both invalidated assertions are loops over run kinds. Deleting the EXPANSION member is correct; deleting the whole case is not, because REVISION must stay provably unsupported on both the create and propose paths. A REVISION path that quietly becomes reachable is exactly the regression DoD 1 forbids.

5. THE FENCE HAS TWO FAILURE DIRECTIONS. A fence that never fires breaks INITIAL's single-node guarantee (DoD 3); a fence that always fires blocks EXPANSION's whole purpose (DoD 2). Drills (d) and (e) test both directions deliberately.

6. AUTHORITY LEAKAGE. DoD 3 forbids any EXPANSION result carrying child run, lease, effect, slot, resource, budget allocation, graph activation, dispatch or partial proposal authority. The accepted EXPANSION state adds exactly two fields — `expansion` and `sealedProposal` — and nothing else. Re-read the diff for this specifically in step 10; it is the one DoD item no test naturally catches.

7. SHARED WORKTREE. All agents work in one directory. `git diff` cannot see the new untracked test file, so never verify a mutation restore by an empty diff. A foreign whole-tree completion hook may commit your in-progress bytes; do not amend, reset or stash (epic rail 3) — report the base-ref diff over owned paths instead. Note task-1df0622e is actively editing graph-revision-*.ts in this same package right now, so a red in src/planning that you did not cause is plausible — attribute it by path before treating it as yours.
